title: Soft-reserve equity allocator for continuous batching (SLO-aware eviction & fair reclaim)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a lightweight soft-reserve equity allocator for our continuous-batching runtime. The allocator enforces latency SLOs while enabling fair GPU memory reclamation and KV cache decay across tenants without harsh preemption spikes. It combines per-tenant credit buckets, decaying reservations for KV working sets, and opportunistic compaction windows so interactive tenants keep latency tails while batchy tenants still get throughput credit.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator can be toggled via runtime feature flag and defaults to disabled
P50/P95 latency for interactive tier unchanged (within +/-5%) on controlled mixed-workload test
KV cache reclaimed under memory pressure with <2x tail-latency amplification compared to baseline preempt path
Fairness: 95th percentile of reclaimed bytes per tenant matches proportional weights within 10% over a 30-minute synthetic run
Automated smoke test coverage added to CI and a perf dashboard panel is created
tasks: Write design doc and cost/benefit analysis
Prototype in runtime: credit buckets, soft-mark eviction, decaying KV reservations
Add admission controller hook for latency-percentile sensing
Implement opportunistic compaction window and selective KV eviction scorer
Bench: mixed interactive+background workload harness with telemetry
Add feature flag, config knobs, and rollout plan
PR + internal review + perf regression signoff
Create dashboard and alert rules for regressions
updates: 2025-02-16: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and product. Agreed to aim for soft-reserve approach to avoid janky preemption behavior.
2025-02-20: Design doc draft uploaded (see design_doc). Early decision: two-phase reclaim (soft-mark then expedited reclaim) to preserve KV locality where possible.
2025-02-28: Prototype credit-bucket simulation shows improved fairness compared to strict FIFO preempt in synthetic traces. Trade-off: ~8% extra CPU for scoring logic.
2025-03-03: Spike testing on a single p4d node identified an edge case where short bursts cause credit starvation; added moving-average weight smoothing to reduce oscillation.
2025-03-05: Began runtime integration PR; basic feature-flag gating and telemetry added. Requesting design review from Sofia Patel and backend review from Mateo Ruiz.
decisions: Use soft-reserve credits (time-decaying) rather than hard reservations to avoid long-term fragmentation of KV cache
Admission controller will use P95 latency window sampled per tenant to switch modes between conservative and aggressive reclaim
Two-phase reclaim: soft-mark to allow background compaction, followed by expedited eviction if memory pressure persists for >800ms
Fairness computed using a waterfilling algorithm with tenant weights and burst-protection multiplier
Fallback: if allocator causes >10% regression on control metrics, automatically disable and revert to existing preemptor
tradeoffs: Pros: smoother tail behavior, better tenant equity over time, fewer large preemption spikes, improved KV locality preservation
Cons: additional CPU/lock contention for scoring, higher implementation complexity, potential for slow gradual memory bleed if decay rates are misconfigured
Mitigations: lightweight scoring, sampling hooks, conservative default decay constants, canary rollout to 5% traffic
risks: Bursting tenants might accumulate credits that starve others during multi-hour windows; addressed by burst-protection multiplier and cooldown windows
Scoring complexity could add jitter to scheduler path; we will measure scheduler latency and keep scoring async where possible
Edge-case regressions when used with Dedicated GPU mixed-tenancy; will require additional stress tests on Dedicated clusters
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on eviction scorer correctness and lock-free paths for the common-case admission checks
Check decay constants for KV reservation; we chose 5-15 minute half-life in draft but want infra input
Validate that telemetry tags provide tenant, priority-tier, and op-type for post-hoc debugging
